scores.claim_text: Azul (Brazilian airline, US-listed ADR CIK 0001432364) committed via term sheet to purchase up to 220 Lilium Jets for $1.0B; Azul Warrants issued Oct 2021; deadline twice extended (Jan 2023, Dec 2023).
scores.supports: Azul's own SEC filings disclose 'Lilium' 4 times across its 20-F filings for FY2021, FY2022, FY2023, and FY2023/A (2022, 2023, 2024 filings). Counterparty corroboration from a US-listed ADR filer confirms the relationship is real and material enough to warrant disclosure in the buyer's annual reports.
scores.interpretation: Counterparty disclosure consistent across all FY periods post-term-sheet. Note: relationship is non-binding and twice-extended — narrative truth confirmed but commercial conversion remains unresolved as of cutoff. PASS for existence-of-relationship; would degrade to MODERATE if framed as committed sale.

scores.claim_text: Bristow Group Inc. (NYSE: VTOL, CIK 0001525221) selected the Lilium Jet for its eVTOL business line in 2022, with rights to order up to 50 Lilium Jets and cooperation on Lilium Florida network maintenance.
scores.supports: Bristow's SEC filings mention 'Lilium' 4 times — all in 8-K investor-presentation exhibits filed Aug-Sep 2022 (the announcement period). No subsequent disclosure in 10-Ks/10-Qs across 2023 or 2024 (within counterparty-corroboration window). For a 50-aircraft commitment from a NYSE-listed counterparty, ongoing program disclosure would be expected if the relationship were progressing materially.
scores.M_value: total_hits=4, all in 8-K investor presentations from Aug-Sep 2022; zero hits in any 10-K, 10-Q, or DEF 14A through cutoff
scores.interpretation: Initial announcement reflected in counterparty filings, but no subsequent disclosure progression — relationship appears static. PASS for original existence; MODERATE for stated current 'developing eVTOL business line' framing 18 months later. Would expect 10-K supply-chain or contractual-commitment language for a real 50-aircraft program.

scores.claim_text: Honeywell Aerospace (HON, CIK 0000773840) partnership with Lilium and DENSO to co-develop and manufacture the electric motor and avionics system for the Lilium Jet.
scores.supports: Honeywell's SEC filings mention 'Lilium' only 2 times across 6+ years of filings (2018-2024), both in DEF 14A proxy statements (2022 and 2024) — not in 10-K business descriptions, 10-Q operations sections, or 8-K product announcements. For a multi-year supply/co-development partnership on a marquee aerospace product, more substantive disclosure footprint would be expected.
scores.interpretation: Per heuristic: Honeywell is enormous ($35B+ revenue) — Lilium-scale supply contracts are immaterial relative to Honeywell's size, so absence from 10-K business sections is expected. However, zero hits in any 10-K is the bottom of the normal range. Borderline PASS/MODERATE — leaning MODERATE given the marketing emphasis Lilium places on Honeywell as a Tier-1 motor/avionics partner.

scores.claim_text: October 2022 non-binding MOU with SAUDIA (Saudi Arabian Airlines Corporation) for purchase of up to 100 Lilium Jets.
scores.supports: SAUDIA is a state-owned, non-US-listed entity that does not file with the SEC. No counterparty registry exists in the M-source catalog for this carrier. Distinctive product 'Lilium Jet' does appear 62 times in EDGAR full-text 6-K filings (mostly Lilium's own); broad search is dominated by self-citation and does not corroborate SAUDIA-specific commitment.
scores.M_value: total_hits=62, predominantly Lilium's own 6-K filings; no SAUDIA-specific corroboration possible via M-sources
scores.interpretation: Per calibration heuristic 1 (foreign issuer / non-US counterparty), state-owned foreign airline disclosure is structurally inaccessible. Cannot be scored as RED_FLAG since the registry mismatch is jurisdictional. Mark UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Non-binding MOU with NetJets Inc. for prospective right to order up to 150 Lilium Jets for fractional ownership program in U.S. and Europe.
scores.supports: NetJets is privately held (Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary). Berkshire Hathaway parent (CIK 0001067983) returned 0 hits for 'Lilium' across all filings. NetJets fleet decisions are immaterial to a $700B+ market cap parent and would not warrant 10-K disclosure.
scores.interpretation: Per heuristic 4 (counterparty wouldn't normally disclose materially) and 7 (private buyer, no SEC filing obligation). The absence is structural, not contradictory. UNVERIFIABLE rather than RED_FLAG. Note: 'non-binding MOU' framing in the claim is appropriately hedged.

scores.claim_text: As of February 2024, Lilium has filed 106 patent families covering propulsion, energy management, power architecture, electric motors, and battery technology.
scores.supports: USPTO ODP returns 13 US-jurisdiction Lilium aviation applications (Lilium eAircraft GmbH 10 + Lilium GmbH 2 + 1 abandoned), filed pre-cutoff. Title categorization shows distribution consistent with claimed tech areas: propulsion/motor (4), battery/energy (8), aircraft systems (20). Specific titles include 'ROTOR FOR A DUCTED FAN ENGINE', 'BATTERY ASSEMBLY ... FOR ELECTRICAL PROPULSION VTOL AIRCRAFT', 'AIRFOIL ... ICE PROTECTION', 'CRASH HANDLING SYSTEM', 'LANDING GEAR FOR VTOL AIRCRAFT', 'ELECTRICAL FAULT ISOLATION IN POWER DISTRIBUTION', 'ELECTRODE ASSEMBLY WITH HEAT SPREADING LAYER'. Subject-matter coverage matches every claimed technology area.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=43, n_granted=26 (includes unrelated 'Lilium Therapeutics' and 'Lilium Candidum'); aircraft-only n_applications=12 with 0 US grants pre-cutoff but 6 granted shortly after; title coverage validates all claimed tech areas
scores.interpretation: Claim was 106 'patent families (first filings)' globally — US is one jurisdiction and Lilium files EU-first per heuristic 8. The 12 US applications with topical breadth across all claimed areas validate the technology-area claim. Zero US grants pre-cutoff is consistent with EU-first filing strategy and 18-24mo USPTO examination lag (6 of 12 granted within 6-15 months post-cutoff). PASS.

scores.claim_text: Order pipeline of 42 binding orders + potential 690 Lilium Jets across 12 countries; distinctive product name 'Lilium Jet' across SEC filings.
scores.supports: EDGAR full-text 'Lilium Jet' across 10-K/10-Q/8-K/DEF 14A/20-F (excluding 6-K) returns only 9 hits — and these are dominated by Lilium's own 20-F filings (4 of 9) and the original Qell SPAC 8-K (1). Three are from XERIANT INC, a microcap unrelated. Effectively only Lilium and its SPAC predecessor mention 'Lilium Jet' in standard US disclosure forms. No US-listed buyer/operator (Bristow, NetJets parent, etc.) names the product in their 10-K business descriptions.
scores.M_value: total_hits=9 — 4 Lilium 20-Fs, 1 Qell SPAC 8-K, 3 Xeriant 10-K (unrelated), 1 other = effectively 5 Lilium-related and 0 third-party operators
scores.interpretation: Per recipe scoring: 1-9 hits = MODERATE; 0 third-party operator/customer 10-K hits despite multi-year, multi-counterparty pipeline narrative. For a real 42-binding-order book, some footprint in operator filings would be expected — but order book is dominated by foreign carriers (Azul, SAUDIA, GlobeAir, AAP, Helity, ASL) and dealerships, which limits US 10-K corroboration. MODERATE rather than SEVERE given the foreign-issuer + foreign-customer structure.

scores.claim_text: Lilium Florida network — Bristow cooperating on maintenance for a Florida-based eVTOL passenger network.
scores.supports: EPA FRS query for 'Lilium' facilities in Florida returns zero. However, an eVTOL passenger network in pre-certification phase (Lilium Jet not type-certified) would not yet have operational ground/airport facilities triggering EPA registration. This is a forward-looking infrastructure claim, not a current operating facility claim.
scores.interpretation: Per heuristic 3 ('Planned facilities EXPECTED empty') and the pre-certification status of the Lilium Jet, absence from EPA FRS is structurally expected. Also, eVTOL passenger operations would be FAA-regulated rather than EPA-regulated. UNVERIFIABLE.

summary.notes: Foreign-issuer profile dominates: 3/8 claims are structurally UNVERIFIABLE due to foreign counterparty (SAUDIA), private counterparty (NetJets/Berkshire), or non-US infrastructure (Florida pre-certification). Two PASS results (Azul ADR corroboration; patent topical coverage). The Honeywell partnership shows weaker-than-expected counterparty footprint (DEF 14A only, no 10-K). Bristow shows 2022-only mention — initial announcement preserved but no escalation, suggesting the 50-aircraft program is not progressing into Bristow's regular disclosure cycle. Order pipeline (C7) shows minimal third-party 10-K corroboration but is consistent with foreign-issuer / foreign-customer structure. Going-concern doubt explicitly noted in audit report. No SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY or RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE within the M-sources available for this foreign-issuer profile.
